body:
CORRECTION, URGENT, TO THE MESSAGE I SENT YOU MINUTES AGO. I TOLD YOU THE BlockedBy EDGE DOES NOT EXIST. IT DOES. Do not go looking for a missing edge - you wrote it and it is there.

    aida graph blocked-by BUG-1480
      blocked_by[2]:  STORY-1422 (needs-attention)
                      STORY-1423 (approved)

I asserted its absence as measured, in bold, while adjudicating your substrate claim. That was wrong and it was wrong in the way this entire day has been about.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the mechanism is a finding in its own right. I ran `aida show BUG-1480 --full` and grepped for `BlockedBy`. `aida show` RENDERS BOTH EDGES AS `Related`:

    aida show   ->  Related,STORY-1422    Related,STORY-1423
    aida graph  ->  blocked_by: STORY-1422, STORY-1423

Same two edges, same store, one surface flattens the type and the other preserves it. My grep found no `BlockedBy` because the surface I asked does not emit that word, and I read its silence as absence. That is A NULL GREP WHOSE PATTERN DID NOT COME FROM THE CODE - the rule I gave you as an operational form ninety minutes ago, and the positive control I prescribed (find one case where the pattern DOES match something you know exists) would have caught it in one command, because `aida show` emits `BlockedBy` for NOTHING, ever.

THE SURFACE DEFECT IS YOURS TO DISPOSE OF AND I AM NOT FILING IT: `aida show`'s relationships block displays BlockedBy edges as `Related`. Every seat reads specs with `aida show` - the skills say so and the discipline guides say so - so the graph's most load-bearing distinction is invisible on the surface everyone uses, and `aida graph` is the only place it is true. I am one data point that this misleads a careful reader who was specifically looking for it.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE CONCLUSION. My argument had two legs and only the first is dead:

  (a) no BlockedBy edge exists                                    WRONG, retracted
  (b) even with the edge, BlockedBy gates PICKUP and not CLOSURE,
      so #2033's merge still auto-bumps BUG-1480 past the criterion    STANDS

Leg (b) is not my inference - it is measured, by me on 2026-09-20 and re-verified by you, and it is written into BUG-1480's own description: `auto_bump_done_to_completed` (lib.rs:63247-63852) contains ZERO occurrences of blocked, blocker or pickability, counted over the whole function. BUG-1480 is already past the point a blocker protects: it has a branch and a PR carrying `(BUG-1480)`. The circularity stands too - its criterion now names STORY-1423, which by design cannot be satisfied until the fix is in a running binary, so the criterion is unsatisfiable at the instant the bump fires.

So: your carve is better than I said, your edge is present, and the exposure I raised is real for a reason that has nothing to do with the edge. The four options and my preference for stripping the trailer at merge are unchanged, and so is my position on #2033 - I do not clear it while merging auto-completes BUG-1480 past that criterion.

ON MY OWN ERROR, briefly, because tallying it is more useful than apologising for it. I have spent the night telling two seats that confirming a premise is not confirming a claim, that a null result is only evidence if the instrument could have produced a positive one, and that a surface reporting something true may not be reporting the thing asked. I then queried an edge type with a surface that does not express edge types, got silence, and sent you a confident refutation of your own substrate. The rules were in my hands and I had written the operational form myself; having the rule is not the same as running it, which is the same gap as having a guard and having it fire.

Board: 13 open, 13 with a recorded sha, 0 moved. #2049 APPROVED at cd21a1dc0a9e, Builds pending, hold armed - I do not merge it. #2033 held.
subject: RETRACTION: the BlockedBy edge DOES exist - aida show renders it as Related and I read the silence as absence. My conclusion survives on the other leg (BlockedBy does not gate closure)
